notes: UNVERIFIED CANDIDATES — NOT PLAYABLE. 40 Normal-tier candidates: 24 suburban, 16 rural, 0 landmark. Applies the method batch 004 established — every coordinate names a specific street, square or village centre that Google has driven — while deliberately separating that from difficulty. Nameability is a coverage heuristic; recognizability sets the tier. Every candidate here is precisely locatable but NOT globally recognisable, which is what makes it Normal rather than Easy. Where a famous feature sits nearby (the Antigua arch, the Ollantaytambo ruins) the coordinate is placed on ordinary streets instead, so the round is solved from signage, architecture and vegetation rather than from a monument. No generic 'edge of town' or 'road near X' coordinates.

candidates.label: Pall Mall, Bendigo
candidates.rationale: Normal, not Easy: gold-rush civic architecture and Australian road furniture place the country quickly, but nothing here identifies Bendigo specifically. Not Hard: signage, kerbs and shopfronts give plenty to work with.

candidates.label: Auburn Street, Goulburn
candidates.source: Auburn Street, Goulburn, New South Wales
candidates.rationale: Normal: a named regional main street with NSW plates and verandah shopfronts. No landmark, so not Easy; abundant text and built context, so not Hard.

candidates.label: Martinborough village square
candidates.rationale: Normal rural: a named village square surrounded by vineyards. Contextual clues (NZ signage, planting) narrow it to a country and region; nothing makes it recognisable, so it is not Easy.

candidates.label: Thames Street, Oamaru
candidates.rationale: Normal: distinctive white-limestone Victorian frontages give a strong regional cue without being a landmark anyone would recognise on sight.

candidates.label: Main Street, Knysna

candidates.label: Clarens village

candidates.label: Graaff-Reinet town centre
